svg.title: "Lost in the middle", and why content-driven heads should help
svg.text: "Lost in the middle", and why content-driven heads should help
schematic: curve shapes only, no measured values
position of the correct tool in a list of 20

g.text: Setup of Liu et al. (2023): the same question, with the one useful item moved from first to last place in a long list.
Start of the list: models do well (primacy: early tokens get extra attention).
Middle: accuracy sags. Some models then do worse than with no list at all.
End: it recovers (recency: the last items sit next to the question). The U shape is "lost in the middle".
plain model: U-shaped (shape from Liu et al.)
Why: a lot of attention is POSITIONAL (sink at the start, recency at the end). It is not about what the item says.
Heads picked because they land on the RIGHT item by content should depend less on position: a flatter curve.
selected heads: flatter (schematic, not your numbers)
Your claim needs your own per-position Recall@1 (not on the server). Without it, say "aimed to mitigate", not "fixed".
